question: Is a verdict a function of the data alone, or does the grouping carry part of it?

expectations.label: lem:dof degrees of freedom set by grouping alone
expectations.prediction: n - |P| depends on P alone and strictly increases along any strictly increasing chain, from 0 at the finest to n-1 at the coarsest.
expectations.failure_mode: A chain along which the denominator fails to increase, or a dependence on x.
expectations.detail: dof [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5] along a strict chain; 0 at finest, 5 at coarsest; identical for two unrelated x

expectations.label: rem:zero-dof the finest grouping computes nothing
expectations.prediction: At the finest grouping the within-group dispersion is undefined --- zero degrees of freedom.
expectations.failure_mode: A finite dispersion at the finest grouping, which would make the remark an edge case rather than a report.
expectations.detail: undefined at the finest grouping, 1.1951 at the coarsest

expectations.label: thm:verdict-depends a refinement flips the verdict
expectations.prediction: There exist x and P1 < P2 whose statistics straddle a fixed threshold; hence no verdict is a function of x alone.
expectations.failure_mode: No (x, threshold) placing the two verdicts on opposite sides, which would leave the verdict a function of x.
expectations.detail: same x: statistic 6.5727 at P1 vs 6.0000 at P2, threshold 6.2863 separates the verdicts

expectations.label: cor:pooling pooling can change the verdict
expectations.prediction: Averaging technical replicates is a coarsening, and by thm:verdict-depends it can change the verdict.
expectations.failure_mode: Pooling that provably never changes a verdict, which would make it a normalisation step after all.
expectations.detail: pooling is a coarsening and moves the statistic 3.5782 -> 3.2385

expectations.label: thm:endpoints two evaluations decide stability
expectations.prediction: For a monotone analysis, agreement at the two endpoints implies agreement everywhere in the interval --- so stability costs 2 evaluations, not |interval|.
expectations.failure_mode: An interval whose endpoints agree but whose interior disagrees under a monotone A.
expectations.detail: 26 intervals, 6 of them unstable, 0 disagreements between the 2-evaluation test and exhaustive enumeration

expectations.label: thm:coarsest-invariant the greatest survivor is permutation-invariant
expectations.prediction: If the survivor set is closed under join it has a greatest element, invariant under every permutation of Obs preserving x.
expectations.failure_mode: A join-closed survivor set with no greatest element, or one moved by an x-preserving permutation.
expectations.detail: join-closed survivor set of 122 groupings has a unique greatest element, fixed by the x-preserving swap r2<->r3

expectations.label: thm:group-floor a positive floor on separation
expectations.prediction: sep(o) >= beta > 0 for every observation, because the medium edge crosses every admissible cut.
expectations.failure_mode: An observation with sep(o) = 0, individuated at no cost.
expectations.detail: beta_0 = 0.5271; min observed sep = 5.2711, all >= beta_0

expectations.label: control: dropping the medium destroys the floor
expectations.prediction: With the medium removed, some observation is individuated at zero cost --- confirming the floor is carried by the medium edge and not by the similarity weights.
expectations.failure_mode: A positive floor surviving removal of the medium, which would make rem:medium's regress argument idle.
expectations.detail: removing the medium leaves a zero-cost separating set (cut = 0.0)

expectations.label: cor:no-free a grouping discards at least beta*(n-|P|)
expectations.prediction: Every grouping coarser than the finest discards a positive quantity, bounded below by beta * (n - |P|).
expectations.failure_mode: A coarsening whose discarded quantity is below the bound.
expectations.detail: finest discards 0; coarsest discards at least 2.6355, monotone along the chain

expectations.label: thm:decline-informative the interval report dominates
expectations.prediction: Two datasets can share a point report while differing in interval report; the interval report determines the point report but not conversely.
expectations.failure_mode: Interval reports that coincide whenever point reports do, making the extra structure idle.
expectations.detail: both report verdict True; intervals of size 5 and 4

expectations.label: cor:degenerate a singleton interval should decline
expectations.prediction: When the survivor interval is exactly {P_top}, the verdict holds at one grouping only and the data do not establish that it is the intended one.
expectations.failure_mode: A singleton interval that nonetheless licenses the point report.
expectations.detail: verdict holds at 1 of 5 admissible groupings (the coarsest alone, statistic 31.08 vs next 25.62); a bare verdict would conceal that 4 groupings disagree

notes: The lattice L(Obs) on 6 observations has 203 elements (Bell(6)); thm:endpoints is what makes that size irrelevant.
Separations are computed by brute-force minimisation over admissible subsets, not by max-flow, so the floor result is checked independently of rem:computable's algorithm.
